correctness.rationale: For every n>=3, occurrence counts of the two length-(L+2) equal-end, alternating-interior factors give E_L=2^(n-L-1) for 1<=L<=n-2. The count of repeat events and exactly two alternating n-factors force either (n,n) or (n-1,n+1) as the remaining gaps. Reading equal pairs synchronizes the three-state greedy scanner; each gap contributes floor(L/2) arches and, for each even gap, exactly L/2 cuts with one missing arch. The two finite sums give K=floor(2^n/3) or ceil(2^n/3) and H=D_n or D_n+n, with all index and cyclic-boundary cases included. This was independently checked against all 2+16+2048 de Bruijn cycles of n=3,4,5, 105 additional random Eulerian cycles and FKM orders 3..10. Direct subsequence search independently checks n=3 and n=4. The proof, not finite tests, covers all orders.

originality.rationale: In the primary full text of Abraham et al. (arxiv:0905.4517), Sections 2-4, de Bruijn cycles are introduced as contiguous universal cycles, while their Waddle Lemma characterizes scattered universality for general words and their subsequent theorems count/estimate random or unrestricted omnibus words. No statement there conditions on de Bruijn cycle membership and classifies universality of all cyclic cuts. The inspected Ruskey-Sawada-Williams 2012 construction targets fixed-weight cyclic substring coverage rather than scattered universality profiles. Bille-Gortz-Skjoldjensen 2015 investigate subsequence automata and size/delay bounds rather than this arithmetic histogram. Searches of publicly published mathematical findings found a full binary-word index generating function, not a conditional two-type de Bruijn theorem. Residual risk of unindexed equivalent formulation remains.

value.rationale: The statement determines a natural, precisely defined quantitative bridge between contiguous universality and scattered-subsequence coverage in every binary de Bruijn cycle. Despite exponentially many possible cycles, every cyclic cut has one of two neighboring indices near one-third of cycle length, and the complete histogram depends only on parity and the position relation of two alternating n-factors. The two-state gap obstruction and exact count are structural all-order information, neither an arbitrary slice nor a known-table recomputation.
